description: This Java source file defines the PdfSurveyServices class, which provides a suite of methods for handling PDF-based surveys within the OFBiz framework. The class includes functions for building surveys from PDFs, extracting and setting form fields, generating survey response PDFs, and managing survey questions and answers. It interfaces with other OFBiz services and entities to manage survey data, responds to form input, and generates PDF documents that represent surveys or survey responses.

classes.name: PdfSurveyServices
classes.description: Utility class providing methods for PDF survey creation, extraction, and response processing within OFBiz.

methods.name: buildSurveyFromPdf
methods.description: Creates a survey entity and associated questions from a PDF form, extracting data from the PDF's form fields using PdfReader and PdfStamper.

methods.name: buildSurveyResponseFromPdf
methods.description: Processes a PDF survey form, extracting user responses, and saves them as SurveyResponseAnswer entities.

methods.name: getAcroFieldsFromPdf
methods.description: Extracts all form fields and their current values from a PDF, returning a map of field names to values.

methods.name: setAcroFields
methods.description: Sets multiple form fields in a PDF document based on the provided map and returns a ByteBuffer with the updated PDF.

methods.name: buildPdfFromSurveyResponse
methods.description: Generates a PDF document representing a survey response, including answers and questions, using iText library.

methods.name: buildSurveyQuestionsAndAnswers
methods.description: Returns a list of survey questions along with their responses for a given survey response ID.

methods.name: setAcroFieldsFromSurveyResponse
methods.description: Updates PDF form fields with data from a survey response, producing a new PDF ByteBuffer, and optionally saves it to a file.

methods.name: getInputByteBuffer
methods.description: Retrieves a ByteBuffer containing PDF data either from a specified file or from content associated with a content ID, within the current context.
